title: include! → mod, slice 2: process_limits as a real module (after host_log lands)
outcome: The process_limits fragment becomes an ordinary Rust module with private state and a minimal pub(crate) facade, in a behaviour-preserving pure move with existing behaviour tests and no source-shape tests, following the w-6296abac468a host_log pattern. Owner Sol-a7bb, as the single owner of src/main.rs declaration-boundary edits. It starts only after host_log (w-6296abac468a) has landed, with a short design (boundary, facade, test count) for coordinator and Kimi review before code. Source: Kimi::Consultant's staged plan (TermAl mailbox 852a55c9 #510) and Greg via Asistant #390.
acceptance: The process file-limit policy lives in an ordinary Rust module with no include bridge. Its sole crate-visible operation is configure_process_open_file_limit, called at the original startup point. All policy helpers, constants, result types and OS adapters are private.

The extraction preserves Unix open-file limit configuration, diagnostic and cap behavior, and the non-Unix no-op. All 26 existing nofile tests pass on the exact candidate with their assertions unchanged.

The exact landed change is a behavior-preserving module move with no source-shape tests. The independent review pair has no outstanding in-scope finding of Medium or higher, and the exact landed input passes the standard full gate.

completion.summary: The process open-file limit policy is an ordinary Rust module (slice 0 of the include! migration, same commit bd01930c155bd15641a6615b37bd87215db02444 as host_log), landed on origin master as the first of the three commits the fast-forward to ebc30de9 carried, pushed 2026-11-22T06:38:30Z by the integration owner on Greg's own word. Review pair S0-PAIR-BD01930C without findings; full gates on bd01930c passed on Linux (test-5db67132) and Windows (test-aef36eb2); the 26 nofile tests passed in the registered run test-3d35b1a9-e25d-4d15-a6c3-beacb5ca7c4b; post-landing evaluation passed all three criteria.
